newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL rubber closes up on covering, Tokyo gains.
newsitem.headline: KL rubber closes up on covering, Tokyo gains.

text.p: The Malaysian rubber market closed higher on local dealers' covering and gains in Tokyo, but the long-term trend is seen bearish, dealers said.

"There were some local dealers' covering. The near-term may look positive," a dealer at a trading house said. "But it all depends on the weather. If it rains in Thailand from mid-August onwards, then we may see prices easing."
Uncertainty in the regional currency movements also cautioned players, dealers said, adding that buyers were keeping to the sidelines while waiting for currencies to stabilise.
There were also covering activities after large purchases by China for July/early August shipment, dealers said.
Some other Far East consumers were also seen checking prices at current levels, they said.
Dealers offered SMR CV at 295 cents, SMR L at 276, SMR 10 at 246, SMR 20 at 245 and latex at 192.
At the close, August RSS1 buyer ended two cents up at 247.50 cents (94 U.S. cents) a kg and August SMR 20 buyer was up 1.50 cents at 246.
